Design

Economy design and tuning

One integer currency, bounded inventories and auditable source/sink rules.

On this page
Canonical dataInitial policiesAffix and set generationReview metricsTransactional examples

Canonical data

Store one base currency balance per character; proposed display100copper=1silver and100silver=1gold uses integer quotient/remainder. Item rarity is a definition/roll result, not a UI color rule. Nonstackable gear has unique instance identity; stack quantity is integer. Item level/prerequisites, binding, durability, affix family restrictions, two-hand exclusion and set bonuses are validated server-side.

Initial policies

Personal loot avoids an early need/greed dispute system. Eligible party members share XP under the declared proximity/contribution rule; personal rolls are stored once. Start deterministic crafting with known outputs. Vendor finite stock/buyback/repair and bank moves share atomic transactions. Direct consensual trade comes after economy tests; auctions remain deferred.

Affix and set generation

Choose allowed affix pools by item family/level and store the rolled values/version on the item instance. Never reroll when loading a tooltip. Enforce nonnegative weights, max affix count and duplicate/exclusive affix rules. Set bonuses derive from equipped definition/set IDs through the same stat-recalculation path; removing a piece removes only its relevant bonus.

Durability loss and repairs are server transactions; broken gear policy must state whether bonuses disable or reduce. Proposal: zero durability disables gear stat bonuses but keeps the visual; tool use rejects BrokenTool. Tooltip displays current/max durability and disabled status. This is a balance proposal, not a verified source-art behavior.

Review metrics

Track currency creation versus sinks, item supply/destroy rates, rare drop distribution, material/time/XP yields, vendor shortages, repair burden, trade reversals and rejected dupes. Do not balance only by increasing prices. Preserve access to required quests/tools and avoid skill choices that permanently prevent main progression.

Transactional examples

Rillmere vendor fixture starts wallet1000, draught50 and stock1; one buy ends950 and one draught. Craft fixture consumes4ore2logs25currency and creates one IronHatchet GUID. Every retry/disconnect/transfer must resolve the same receipt. Cost and loot values remain tunable in definitions, never hardcoded in UMG.

Planned game assets are not compiled assets. Values are proposals unless explicitly evidenced. Verification and limitations.
